title: Kaikeyi's boons
hook: Rama rides to his coronation through cheering streets, and finds his father unable to speak
carry: the king says one word: Rama

segments.voice: Yesterday: the longest night. The king begged, and Kaikeyi held him to satya, a word that holds. Today, morning comes.

Outside the palace, nobody knows. The sun rises on the morning Ayodhya has prepared for. Vasishtha arrives with his students and the sacred waters. The streets are full. Bards sing outside the king's door to wake him, as they do every morning. Inside, the king hasn't slept, and he can't stand up. Two worlds, one wall, and in a moment Rama will walk from one into the other.
screen: `OUTSIDE, NOBODY KNOWS.` → `BARDS SING AT THE KING'S DOOR.` → `TWO WORLDS, ONE WALL.`

segments.voice: The charioteer Sumantra goes in to say everything is ready. The king can barely speak. Kaikeyi answers for him: bring Rama here. Sumantra, puzzled, goes. Rama rides through packed streets and hears the people as he passes: today he'll be made heir; how fortunate we are. Women lean from windows to see him. In Kaikeyi's room he finds his father on a couch, pale, beside the queen. Rama bows to his father's feet, then to Kaikeyi's. The king manages one word, Rama, and then his eyes fill and he can't say more. Rama has never seen his father like this. Frightened, he turns to Kaikeyi. Have I done something wrong? Is he ill? Has someone hurt him? The king won't speak, she says, because he's afraid to tell you something unpleasant. He made me a promise. If you'll do what he promised, I'll tell you. And Rama, not knowing what's coming, says something he can't take back. At my father's word I would walk into fire. I would drink poison. Tell me what he wants. I promise to do it, and Rama doesn't say things twice. So Kaikeyi tells him, plainly. Bharata consecrated with the waters made ready for Rama. Rama to the Dandaka forest for fourteen years, in bark clothes, with matted hair. Notice who says it. Not the king, who lies there unable to speak. The boons arrive in Kaikeyi's voice, to a son who has just promised to obey.
screen: `SUMANTRA SENT TO FETCH RAMA.` · `THE KING SAYS ONE WORD: RAMA.` · `RAMA PROMISES BEFORE HE KNOWS.` · `KAIKEYI TELLS HIM HERSELF.` · then, large: `RAMA DOESN'T SAY THINGS TWICE.`

segments.voice: Bring back a moment just before hard news, if you've had one: the room, the faces, the silence. Breathe in and let the body brace a little, the way it does; breathe out and let the bracing go. Do it once more, gently, practicing the moment before, so you can meet it standing.
Kaikeyi's boons, delivered. The king can only say Rama's name, so Kaikeyi tells Rama herself: Bharata crowned, and fourteen years in the forest.
Your line: the king says one word: Rama. Tomorrow, we hear how Rama answers. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: In the text, Rama's phrase that he does not say things twice comes before he knows what he has agreed to; it is a picture of a person whose word is final.

fork.setup: you're Rama. your father can't speak, and the queen says she'll explain only if you promise to obey. what do you say?
options: first tell me what it is.
I promise; Rama doesn't say things twice.
fork.reveal: Rama promises at once: at his father's word he would walk into fire or drink poison.

original.note: Sanskrit pratijñā: a promise, a vow. Rama gives one before he hears what it will cost.

trapdoor: what you thought: the king sends Rama away himself.
what it means: the king can't speak, and Kaikeyi tells Rama the boons.
what a scholar hears: Rama's half-verse about not speaking twice is spoken before he knows the cost, so his promise binds him the way his father's oath bound the king.

chat.says: Why does Kaikeyi break the news to Rama, and not his father?
options: The king is so broken he can only say Rama's name, so she tells him.
The king has already left the palace to hide from Rama's anger.
Rama refuses to hear it from anyone but the queen who raised him.
chat.meaning: Dasharatha manages only one word, Rama, then can't go on. The boons reach Rama in Kaikeyi's voice.

Vasishtha.meaning: the royal family's priest and teacher

Dandaka.meaning: the great forest of Rama's exile
